extracted.intended_audience: R package authors, reviewers, and editors participating in rOpenSci Software Peer Review
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and criteria for submitting, reviewing, onboarding, maintaining, and removing R packages in the rOpenSci software peer review system, including scope, ethical expectations, COI rules, and maintainer responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process — submission and review flow
rubrics_metrics.description: For a package to be considered for the rOpenSci suite, package authors must initiate a request on the ropensci/software-review repository. Packages are reviewed for quality, fit, documentation, clarity and the review process is quite similar to a manuscript review. Unlike a manuscript review, this process will be an ongoing conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication between authors, reviewers and editors will first and foremost take place on GitHub (authors should ensure GitHub notifications are set so they won't miss comments). An assigned editor will make a decision (accept, hold, or reject) once major issues and reasonable-effort items are resolved. Rejections are usually done early (before review begins), but may occur after review. Authors may request holding status; holding label is revisited every 3 months and after one year the issue will be closed. If authors do not respond and have not requested hold, the issue should be closed within one month after the last contact intent — contact intent must include a comment tagging the author and an email to the address in DESCRIPTION. If closed, resubmission requires starting a new submission and responding to initial reviews before the editor seeks new reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing in other venues
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly suggested to submit their package for rOpenSci review before publishing on CRAN or submitting a software paper describing the package to a journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review feedback may result in major improvements (renaming, breaking changes). Previous publication on CRAN or elsewhere is not sufficient reason to ignore reviewer/editor recommendations. Do not submit your package for rOpenSci review while it or an associated manuscript is under review at another venue, to avoid conflicting change requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest (COI) for reviewers/editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Guiding criteria for what constitutes a conflict of interest for an editor or reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A potential reviewer/editor has a COI if: they are from the same institution or institutional component (e.g., department) as any author with a major role; they have been a collaborator or had other professional relationships with at least one person on the package who has a major role within the past three years; they serve or have served as a member of the advisory board for the project under review; they would receive a direct or indirect financial benefit if the package were accepted; they have significantly contributed to a competitor project. There is also a lifetime COI for family members, business partners, and thesis student/advisor or mentor. If no associate editors can serve, recruit an external guest editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope — overall remit
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci aims to support packages that enable reproducible research and manage the data lifecycle for scientists. Packages should fit into one or more specified categories; statistical software has a separate set of guidelines and standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories are a living list and may change; not all previously onboarded packages would be in-scope today. Evaluate packages case-by-case and allow exceptions. If unsure whether a package fits, open a pre-submission inquiry issue. Note some rOpenSci projects (staff or conference projects) may be experimental and not pass through peer review; look for the peer-review badge to identify peer-reviewed packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: data retrieval packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages for accessing and downloading data from online sources with scientific applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retrieval packages should be focused on data sources or topics, and should do more than just download data. General clients for services (e.g., AWS data storage) or packages that only offer download functionality without pre-processing/pre-filtering are out of scope. Examples: rotl (wide range of functions), gutenbergr (pre-processes metadata).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: data extraction packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages that aid in retrieving data from unstructured sources such as text, images and PDFs, and parsing scientific data types and outputs from scientific equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical/ML modelling libraries or general code parsers are typically not included. Trained models that act as utilities (e.g., OCR utilities) may qualify. Examples: tabulizer, genbankr, treeio, lightr.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: data munging packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages for processing data from the formats above focused on specific scientific formats generated from workflows or instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include broad data manipulation tools (e.g., reshape2, tidyr) or tools for extracting data from R code itself. Examples: plateR, phonfieldwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: data deposition packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages that support deposition of data into research repositories, including data formatting and metadata generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: EML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: data validation and testing packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools that enable automated validation and checking of data quality and completeness as part of scientific workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: assertr.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: workflow automation packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools that automate and link together workflows, such as build systems and tools to manage continuous integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include general tools for literate programming (e.g., R Markdown extensions unless tightly tied to workflow automation). Example: drake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: version control packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools that facilitate the use of version control in scientific workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include all tools that interact with online version control services (e.g., GitHub) unless they fit into another category. Example: git2rdata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: citation management and bibliometrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools that facilitate managing references, CV creation, attribution, or accessing/manipulating bibliometric data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: RefManageR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: scientific software wrappers
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages that wrap non-R utility programs used for scientific research and must be non-trivial wrappers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wrappers must add significant value beyond simple system() calls or bindings (parsing inputs/outputs, data handling, improved installation or platform support). Do not include wrappers of other R packages or C/C++ libraries that can be included in R packages. Prefer wrapping open-source/open-licensed utilities; exceptions evaluated case-by-case. Does not include web API clients which must fit other categories. Examples: babette, nlrx.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: field and laboratory reproducibility tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages that improve reproducibility of real-world workflows through standardization and automation of field and lab protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes sample tracking/tagging, form and data sheet generation, interfacing with lab equipment or information systems, and executing experimental designs. Example: baRcodeR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: database software bindings
rubrics_metrics.description: Bindings and wrappers for generic database APIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: rrlite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: specialty topics (geospatial, translation, internal tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special interest categories accepted with slightly broader scope: geospatial data, translation tools for multilingual publishing, and rOpenSci internal tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geospatial: packages for accessing/manipulating/converting geospatial data (examples: osmplotr, tidync). Translation: interfaces to automated translation, frameworks for managing documentation in multiple languages, or accessing linguistic resources — experimental; open a pre-submission inquiry. rOpenSci internal tools: packages created/used by rOpenSci to support review and initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other scope considerations — generality and interactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages should be general: solve a problem broadly while maintaining a coherent user interface and code base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If several data sources use an identical API, prefer a package providing access to all sources rather than just one. Packages that include interactive tools (e.g., shiny apps) must provide a mechanism to make the interactive workflow reproducible (code generation or scriptable API). If out-of-scope for rOpenSci, consider CRAN, BioConductor, cloudyr, JOSS, JSS, or R Journal depending on scope. Note internal rOpenSci-developed packages may not be in-scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package overlap / duplication considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci aims to avoid duplication of functionality of existing R packages unless a package significantly improves on alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A package that replicates existing functionality may be included if it significantly improves on alternatives by being: more open in licensing or development practices; broader in functionality (but not merely duplicating additional packages); better in usability and performance; actively maintained while alternatives are poorly or no longer actively maintained. Consider these factors as a whole. New packages should highlight differences/improvements in README and/or vignettes. Developers of non-accepted overlapping packages are encouraged to submit elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package ownership and role of rOpenSci team
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors retain ownership and will continue to maintain their software after acceptance; rOpenSci will not interfere with day-to-day operations unless explicitly added as collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: rOpenSci may intervene for critical bug fixes or address urgent issues if authors do not respond in a timely manner (see maintainer responsiveness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintainer responsiveness and remediation timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If maintainers do not respond in a timely manner to requests for fixes from CRAN or rOpenSci, rOpenSci will remind maintainers but may make changes themselves after 3 months (or sooner for critical fixes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples where rOpenSci would move quickly: a package imported by CRAN packages breaks reverse dependencies; a widely used package is broken even without reverse dependencies. Examples where they can wait: packages not on CRAN or with no reverse dependencies, or maintainers who have responded but are temporarily busy. Authors should ensure GitHub notifications and email from rOpenSci/CRAN are not filtered to spam. Onboarded package authors will be invited to rOpenSci Slack. If authors abandon maintenance of an actively used package, rOpenSci may petition CRAN to transfer maintainer status to rOpenSci.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality commitment and continued support
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci strives to develop and promote high quality research software and reviews all submissions as part of Software Peer Review and may continue to step in after acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite support, errors remain the responsibility of individual maintainers. Buggy or unmaintained software may be removed from the suite at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package removal and archival rights
rubrics_metrics.description: In the scenario that a contributor requests removal of their package from the suite, rOpenSci retains the right to maintain a version of the package in their suite for archival purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics expectation — general
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci expects tools to enable ethical use by research practitioners; software developers must consider ethical use of their products and adhere to professional ethical codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developers should place themselves in researchers' role and consider requirements of an ethical workflow. Given variability in internet-based analyses, judgment calls are required. Adherence to legal/regulatory minimums (e.g., GDPR) may not be sufficient. Authors should direct users to relevant ethical resources. Editors may require additional (or reduced) functionality, robust documentation, defaults, and warnings for packages that merit enhanced scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics meriting enhanced ethical scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific topics that may require enhanced scrutiny: vulnerable populations; personally identifiable or sensitive data (including 'reasonably re-identifiable' data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For these packages, editors may require extra documentation, defaults, warnings, or changes to functionality to direct users to relevant ethical practices and minimize risk of harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to data source terms and scraping limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages should adhere to data source’s terms of use, robots.txt files, privacy policies, and other relevant restrictions, and link to them prominently in package documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Packages should provide or document functionality to adhere to such restrictions (e.g., scrape only allowed endpoints, use appropriate rate limiting in code, examples, or vignettes). Note that Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policies may not provide sufficient ethical bounds but can provide an outer bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent and data acquisition support
rubrics_metrics.description: Package authors should support users' acquisition of informed consent when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may include providing links to data source's preferred consent methods, contact information of data providers (e.g., forum moderators), documentation of informed consent protocols, or pre-approval for general uses of a package. Reminder: consent is not implicitly granted because data are accessible; accessible data are not necessarily public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security best practices and de-identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages accessing or handling personally identifiable or sensitive data should follow security best practices (e.g., secure internet protocols, strong credential storage) and enable/document/demonstrate workflows for de-identification and secure storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should demonstrate how their package minimizes risk of harm via de-identification workflows, secure storage, and other best practices. As standards evolve, authors may attach ethics approvals or other documentation to submission threads or convey them to editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics resources and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Helpful resources for addressing ethical questions related to privacy and research software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References explicitly mentioned: Declaration of Helsinki; The Belmont Report; Ethical Guidelines of The Association of Internet Researchers; NESH Guide to Internet Research Ethics; BPS' Ethics Guidelines for Internet-Mediated Research; and a list of scholarly articles and overviews (Anabo et al. 2019; Bechmann & Kim 2019; Chu et al. 2021; Lomborg & Bechmann 2014; Flick 2016; Sugiura et al. 2017; Taylor & Pagliari 2018; Zimmer 2010). Authors, editors, and reviewers are encouraged to consult these when evaluating ethical aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci has a Code of Conduct that applies to all people participating in the rOpenSci community, including staff and leadership, and to all modes of interaction online or in person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code of Conduct is maintained on the rOpenSci website and applies to contributors, reviewers, editors, and other participants.
